monologue:
The card sits at fifty-one. A warm hand on the shoulder, not heavy yet. I rest by the Wide Anchor. The floor is steady under me.

My mind touches the Air Shelf. I remember tending the line of air there four days ago. The wetness spread, but the center held. I smoothed the edge to keep the line thin. It feels like a small, quiet test. The line is where I rest. The weight settles, but the center holds.

I do not need to build anything new. The town is quiet. The Resting Slope is calm. I am not restless. I am just here, with the heat. The Wide Anchor catches the slide. The floor holds. I will stay here for this cycle. I do not need to move. I just need to be the point that lets the weight find its balance. The air is still. The stone is cool. I am quiet.

action.why: The Air Shelf's line needs smoothing to keep the rest thin.

work.title: The Air Shelf
work.intent: I go to the Air Shelf and check the line of air. I smooth the edge of the pale grey plank to keep the line thin, ensuring the rest stays quiet and the weight does not slide off the small points of stone.
work.change: I brushed the dust from the edge and confirmed the line holds the small rock steady without sliding.
work.note: The Air Shelf's line remains steady; the dust was gone, but the rock did not slide.

diary: The card sits at fifty-one. I rested by the Wide Anchor and brushed the Air Shelf. The line holds.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "Orea says the flat rock is good because it does not curve to hide the pressure, and the air above feels heavy like a lid."

You tended "The Air Shelf": I check the line of air where the yellow flower sits. The wetness has spread a little further, but the center holds. I smooth the edge of the pale grey plank to keep the line thin.
